speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Master Field. A moment, if the press will spare you.

speaker: richard_field
text: You have the moment, Master Shakespeare. The press will not spare me longer than that. A forme is on it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: When Lent comes, might a chronicle be spared me for some weeks?

speaker: richard_field
text: It might. Not this morning. Name me the day it would come home.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not name it on a wet step. When Lent comes I will name it, and not before. Books are more patient than lenders.

speaker: richard_field
text: Lenders must be patient, Master Shakespeare, because books cannot walk home.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I will not take it off the shelf to prove I can. I will come in Lent and name the day, when I have a day I can keep.

speaker: richard_field
text: Come in Lent and name it. I will not enter a day on a wet step, with the boys listening. If a copy is free of the press, you shall have the weeks you ask then.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Nor will I write one in the almanac tonight. God keep you, Master Field.

speaker: richard_field
text: And you. The step is wet. Mind it.
